convoLines.text: "Can we talk?" Imani shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Imani. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it. There. Said it."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you believe in. I'm listening."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"Still on what scares you most."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
At the hollow the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Leroy's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "I dreamed Tanisha was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Tanisha said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Tanisha. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me yes, once. No details. I haven't forgotten. I just don't ask."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Please — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. I need help. Please."
"Rest won't touch this. The heat's climbing and my head's full of cotton. Someone who knows what they're doing — please."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Leroy: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
"Please — whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Will you help me?"
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Still on that favor."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Tanisha always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about that favor — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?'"
"It's already handled. Thank you for asking."
"As I said — Still on that favor."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"No, really — it's handled. Thanks for asking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"Still on what day it is."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? That's the whole of it."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I know you and Rosa were close. I'm sorry."
"I keep turning over the last thing Rosa said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you believe we get through this — the alternative doesn't work. Still holding the line?"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
Carlos looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want the truth? I'm not from Denver. I'm from Veracruz, Mexico. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others. Happy now?"
"We went over this," Carlos says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Wanjiru sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Wanjiru has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Still on where you're from. Anyway, that's me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on how this changed you."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to keep everyone fed. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Gladys rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"That again?" Gladys sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
